chapter: George Lewis and the 1946 Jazz Foundation concert
title: Advertising wagon and the 1946 Louis Armstrong concert
summary: Williams explains the advertising wagon for the National Jazz Foundation concert the night Louis Armstrong was in town; Kid Howard played the wagon and they kept Bunk Johnson sober that day.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Huh? Clinet. Mostly clarinet. Okay. He's a, he was a good man on it. I just heard him play it a few times. He got around him. Well, tell me about that advertisement you had on the wagon. How did that happen? Um, I, uh, I, uh, I, uh, advertised for this guy here on Degenfield Street.
Dick is, uh, the potato chips? Dick is potato chips.
No, the one for the National Jazz Foundation.
They had Louis here you say?

Louis Armstrong was here, yeah. That's the night he turned Basin Street around. When they turned Basin Street around? Changed the name of it, huh? Yeah, changed around. Well, they kept Bunk Johnson all day at my house, keeping him out from getting drunk. And on the advertising they used Howard.
Yeah, they keep him straight for that concert that night because there's people that spend plenty of money tonight. That was in 1946, that's the time they put us in the local.
They had a sold out house.
